text.title: Market Research TAM SAM SOM Decision Tree
text.summary: Routes on whether a unit of consumption is nameable, whether both a bottom-up build and a top-down cross-check exist, and whether their divergence exceeds 2x — to a full TAM/SAM/SOM run, a blocked sign-off pending reconciliation, or a skip when the arithmetic has nothing to stand on.

decision-tree.root-question: Can a unit of consumption be named — a countable set of addressable buyers or units, and a realised price per unit?

branch.when: no pricing hypothesis and no countable buyer population — or a created category with no existing budget line to count against

conclusion.verdict: skip; bottom-up is impossible and a top-down figure alone is not an output. Route to jtbd-switch-interview to find the budget line the buyer is already spending against

branch.when: an addressable unit count and a realised price per unit are each independently sourceable
branch.question: Which estimates are actually in hand — a bottom-up build, a third-party top-down figure, or both?

branch.when: only a published analyst or third-party top-down figure exists; nothing has been built from units and price

conclusion.verdict: do not publish the analyst figure as TAM; build bottom-up as unit count multiplied by realised annual price, then keep the top-down number as the cross-check

branch.when: both a bottom-up build and a top-down cross-check exist and their ratio can be computed
branch.question: Is the ratio between the two methods greater than 2x?

branch.when: the two methods diverge by more than 2x

conclusion.verdict: block sign-off; name the specific differing term — unit definition, price basis, geography or timeframe — and restate one method under the other's assumption before anything downstream uses the number

branch.when: the two methods agree within 2x and the ratio is recorded

conclusion.verdict: apply the full methodology; quantify each SAM filter separately with its own retained fraction, bound SOM against a capacity model rather than a share of SAM, and keep at most one forecast layer in any chain
